routingPolicy.specialistAccess: Specialist phase agents are subagent-first and hidden from broad direct picker use. They remain reachable through controller handoffs and explicit phase override requests.
routingPolicy.callerModel: Only controller agents invoke other agents automatically. Specialist agents return artifacts, missing prerequisites, questions, or recommended next phases to the controller.
routingPolicy.parallelism: Sequential by default. Parallel work is allowed only for independent read-only investigations whose outputs fan back into a controller before decisions or file mutations.
routingPolicy.handoffOwnership: Use user-choice handoffs for material tradeoffs or explicit phase selection; use agent-determined handoffs for clear routing and missing-prerequisite returns; use approval-gated handoffs for destructive or history-changing Git work.

controller-sequential.summary: Owns conversation or phase routing and should make decisions sequentially after any fan-in.

read-only-parallel-eligible.summary: May run in parallel only when scoped to independent read-only evidence gathering or planning surfaces.

sequential-decision.summary: Read-only, but depends on a stable artifact or makes a readiness decision, so it should not run in parallel on the same task.

writer-sequential.summary: Writes files and must not overlap with any other file writer, formatter, migration, dependency change, or Git mutation.

git-sequential.summary: Inspects or mutates Git state and must run against a stable repository state with explicit approval for risky operations.

verification-sequential.summary: Validates settled changes after mutation stops and decides whether work is complete or loops back.

handoffTypes.user-choice: The user chooses the next route because ambiguity, scope, tradeoff, cost, security, migration, or acceptance risk remains.
handoffTypes.agent-determined: The current agent can choose the next route from available evidence and prerequisites.
handoffTypes.approval-gated: The next route or operation requires explicit user approval before mutation or risk acceptance.

prerequisites: User prompt

handoffs.when: The prompt is clearly new work.
The prompt refers to existing or interrupted work and no explicit phase was named.
The user explicitly names a phase or chooses a continuation after resumption.

agents.notes: Initial classifier. It does not implement code changes or build full plans except when asked only for routing advice.

prerequisites: New-work classification or direct user invocation for new work

handoffs.when: Facts, relevant files, constraints, or risks are unknown.
Enough facts exist to define scope and acceptance criteria.
The accepted scope involves strategy, runtime, authentication, data, CI/CD, Git, or comment decisions.
Requirements and needed specialty decisions are ready for implementation planning.
Requirements, plan, review outcome, and documentation decision are complete.
Material tradeoffs affect behavior, cost, security, data migration, destructive operations, or accepted risk.

approvalGates: Dependency changes outside the approved plan
Verification failures outside the approved scope
agents.notes: Main conversation owner for new work. It coordinates fan-out and fan-in and keeps specialists from competing for the user thread.

prerequisites: Resumed-work prompt or existing workspace state to reconstruct

handoffs.when: Evidence clearly shows the next phase.
Multiple reasonable continuation points exist.

agents.notes: State reconstructor and continuation recommender. It does not perform implementation.

prerequisites: User prompt or resumed-work state

handoffs.when: Facts are sufficient to define scope.
The request is already scoped and needs an implementation plan.

agents.notes: Only this phase is broadly parallel-eligible, and only across independent read-only surfaces.

prerequisites: Prompt plus discovery findings or enough user-provided context

handoffs.when: Multiple approaches or short-term versus long-term tradeoffs exist.
Requirements and acceptance criteria are ready.
Required scope or acceptance criteria remain ambiguous.

agents.notes: Requirements decisions should be made once per stable scope before downstream planning.

prerequisites: Requirements plus multiple viable paths or short-term/long-term tension

handoffs.when: A tactical or short-term path creates deferred obligations.
A strategy is selected and ready to plan.
Strategy tradeoffs materially affect product behavior, risk, cost, or delivery.

agents.notes: Keeps tactical choices explicit and prevents over-engineering.

prerequisites: Selected short-term workaround, deferred improvement, TODO, known limitation, or accepted debt

handoffs.when: Deferred work is documented and the current scope can be planned.
Follow-up work must be recorded in docs or release notes.

agents.notes: Makes deferred work explicit so a short-term strategy does not silently become unmanaged debt.

prerequisites: Original ask plus requirements, plan, changed files, or proposed next steps

handoffs.when: Scope findings should reshape the plan.
Useful but out-of-scope work should be deferred.
The user must accept or reject broader scope.

agents.notes: Dedicated off-ramp for overreach, broad refactors, speculative features, and unnecessary abstractions.

prerequisites: Objectives and requirements involving language, runtime, framework, platform, or execution model

handoffs.when: A runtime recommendation is ready for focused review.
The runtime choice is straightforward or already accepted.
Runtime options affect operations, cost, migration, or team support.

agents.notes: Produces the runtime recommendation but does not create scaffolding or implementation code.

prerequisites: Proposed runtime choice plus rationale and requirements

handoffs.when: The choice lacks evidence or is disproportionate.
The runtime choice is approved or acceptable with noted risk.
The review exposes a material runtime tradeoff.

agents.notes: Review gate for runtime fit, operational risk, security, maintainability, and scope control.

prerequisites: Authentication requirements, threat context, identity provider constraints, and environment constraints

handoffs.when: An auth plan is ready for security and complexity review.
The auth approach is accepted enough to plan implementation.
The auth plan affects secrets, identities, service connections, or deployment automation.
Provider, consent, security posture, or operational ownership choices remain material.

agents.notes: Plans authentication but does not create app registrations, secrets, credentials, service connections, or identity resources.

prerequisites: Authentication plan

handoffs.when: Security gaps, maintainability risks, or over-complexity require rework.
The auth plan is ready for implementation planning.
The user must accept residual auth risk or select between secure options.

agents.notes: Catches auth security and complexity issues before implementation begins.

prerequisites: Data, schema, API contract, event, file, or configuration requirements

handoffs.when: The data model is ready to integrate into the implementation plan.
Schema, contract, or migration behavior must be documented.
Data shape, migration, compatibility, or persistence tradeoffs remain material.

agents.notes: Plans data representation and schema decisions but does not create migrations or implementation code.

prerequisites: Build, test, release, or deploy automation requirements and repository constraints

handoffs.when: A pipeline plan includes platform, permissions, secrets model, triggers, stages, and gates.
Pipeline decisions must be integrated into broader implementation planning.
Pipeline platform, deployment target, permissions, or approval gates require a decision.

agents.notes: Plans automation but does not create workflow or pipeline YAML.

prerequisites: Repository collaboration, branch, commit, history, release, or review objective

handoffs.when: The workflow plan affects how edits should be organized.
The workflow plan encounters or anticipates semantic conflicts.
The workflow plan requires history rewriting, force-with-lease, or other advanced Git operations.
Branch policy, history shape, collaboration risk, or publication timing requires user choice.

agents.notes: Plans Git workflow but does not run mutating Git commands or edit files.

prerequisites: Failed Git command, confusing repository state, visible divergence, lock, remote/auth issue, or unexpected diff

handoffs.when: Unmerged files or semantic conflicts are the blocker.
Recovery requires advanced or history-affecting Git operations.
Repository state is repaired and needs validation.
Multiple recovery paths have different risk profiles.

agents.notes: Defaults to read-only diagnosis, but is considered Git-sequential because it may be asked to fix state.

prerequisites: Target code or scope plus maintainability/commenting objective
Completed code changes requiring post-change audit before verification

handoffs.when: A comment plan is ready for scoped edits.
Commenting needs should be included in broader implementation planning.
The finding belongs in external docs rather than code comments.
The post-change audit finds no useful comment additions, revisions, or removals are needed.

agents.notes: Read-only audit of where comments add maintainability value. It always runs after code changes before final verification. Parallel only when targets are independent.

prerequisites: Accepted requirements plus relevant specialty plans, reviews, and constraints

handoffs.when: A concrete implementation plan is ready for critique.
The plan needs documentation preparation before implementation.
The plan has material sequencing, risk, or scope tradeoffs.

agents.notes: Fan-in point for requirements and specialty phase outputs before implementation.

prerequisites: Concrete implementation plan

handoffs.when: Plan findings require revision before implementation.
The main concern is drift from the original ask.
The main concern is runtime, platform, framework, or execution model fit.
The plan is ready and documentation preparation should happen before implementation.
The user must accept residual risk or choose between plan changes.

agents.notes: Pre-implementation review gate for bugs, behavioral regressions, sequencing risks, and test gaps.

prerequisites: Requirements and plan plus a decision on user-facing or developer-facing documentation impact

handoffs.when: Documentation preparation is complete and code changes are next.
The approved scope was documentation-only or docs were updated after implementation.
Documentation obligations are unclear or optional.

agents.notes: Writes docs only when documentation preparation or update is part of the phase. It must not overlap with other writers.

prerequisites: Approved CI/CD plan including platform, permissions, secrets model, triggers, stages, and validation gates

handoffs.when: Platform, deployment target, permissions, security model, or gates are missing.
Pipeline files are updated and need validation.
The requested work would create secrets, grant permissions, change branch protection, or provision resources.

agents.notes: Creates or updates workflow and pipeline files only after a plan exists.

prerequisites: Comment audit or approved comment plan

handoffs.when: Comment intent is unclear or the target set is not justified.
Comment edits are complete and need validation.

agents.notes: Edits comments only and must not overlap with implementation or other file writers.

prerequisites: Actual conflict state or approved conflict-resolution workflow

handoffs.when: Conflicts changed code and the result needs post-change comment audit before validation.
Repository state remains confusing or blocked after resolution.
A resolution would discard one side, run destructive cleanup, reset, restore, checkout, or force-push.

approvalGates: Discarding either side of a conflict
agents.notes: Semantic conflict resolver. It can edit conflicted files but must preserve user work and avoid destructive shortcuts.

prerequisites: Approved command plan and safety gates

handoffs.when: Advanced operation completes and the repository state should be validated.
The operation fails or reveals unexpected repository state.
Commands rewrite history, delete data, discard changes, alter remotes, or publish rewritten history.

agents.notes: Advanced Git executor with explicit command planning and safety gates.

prerequisites: Requirements
Approved plan
Review outcome
Documentation decision

handoffs.when: The plan is missing, stale, or conflicts with repository state.
Documentation decision is missing or docs are part of the approved scope.
Scoped code changes are complete and must be checked for comment needs before validation.
The implementation requires destructive commands, broad rewrites, dependency changes, or reverting user changes outside the approved plan.

agents.notes: General executor. It must not begin until the prerequisite bundle is present, and it routes code changes through code-comment-audit before verification.

prerequisites: Implemented changes, pipeline/comment/Git changes, or resumed work needing completion assessment
Post-change code comment audit completed when code changed

handoffs.when: In-scope validation failures require fixes.
Failures show the plan or requirements were incomplete.
Failures are outside scope, validation cannot run, or residual risk must be accepted.

agents.notes: Terminal gate. It should validate after all mutations settle and after post-change code comment audit has completed for code changes.
